requested_outcome: Create, verify and publish direct legacy-to-new VII URL handling for every discoverable old URL, using 301 only when a real equivalent exists and 410 when no equivalent exists.
authorization_boundary: Read old and new sitemaps and the authenticated VII Search Console property; change VII redirect code, tests and administration; publish the verified release and prepare the old-domain cutover. Do not invent equivalents, redirect obsolete content to the home page, alter unrelated catalogs, or claim the old domain is migrated before live DNS/runtime evidence proves it.

lesson_bundle.reason: The request follows repeated completion and publication corrections.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Completion must be proven at the live old URL, not inferred from code or a deployment queue.

lesson_bundle.reason: Redirects affect every old entry route and crawler state.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Exact, variant, missing, asset, query, 410 and chain behavior must be tested across the affected family.

lesson_bundle.reason: The desired result requires a production runtime and domain cutover.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Record immutable release identity, rollback target and live HTTP evidence on both hostnames.

lesson_bundle.reason: The task is an organic-search migration with canonical and indexation consequences.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Each old URL must resolve in one hop to a semantically equivalent indexable canonical or an intentional 410.

lesson_bundle.reason: Redirect ownership must remain manageable after migration.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: The administration redirect source must actually participate in public request resolution and prevent chains.

lesson_bundle.reason: The existing redirect screen is not evidence that public traffic uses its records.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Create/update/disable behavior must be verified through the public worker, with audit-friendly deterministic precedence.

predicted_rejections.rejection: Only sitemap URLs are covered while valuable historical Search Console URLs are missed.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Build the source inventory from the old sitemap, authenticated Search Console evidence, catalog source URLs and explicit legacy routes.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: The inventory report states counts and disposition for every collected source, with zero unclassified sitemap URLs.

predicted_rejections.rejection: The code says 301 but live www.vii.co.il still serves the old page.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Treat domain attachment/cutover as part of delivery and test the old hostname directly after release.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Representative old URLs return HTTP 301 from www.vii.co.il in one hop to final new 200 canonical URLs.

predicted_rejections.rejection: Old pages are dumped onto the home page or into redirect chains.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Require semantic targets, reject home catch-all and resolve targets to final canonical paths before publication.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Automated audit finds no home catch-all, no loop and no multi-hop chain among classified URLs.

predicted_rejections.rejection: The admin redirects UI exists but its records do not affect public requests.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Wire D1 redirect lookup into the worker ahead of static legacy fallback with strict normalization and status handling.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Worker tests prove enabled 301 and 410 records, disabled records, precedence and safe fallback behavior.

predicted_rejections.rejection: Publication breaks assets, locale URLs, sitemap or current public routes.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Scope legacy matching to old page routes and run full build plus public-route, sitemap, robots, asset and locale regression checks.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Exact release passes tests and live checks for old hosts, new hosts, sitemap index, robots, assets and representative localized pages.

affected_family: all 2,711 URLs in the legacy sitemap
historical VII URLs visible in Search Console
legacy vacation, event and hourly place pages
legacy category, search and filtered landing pages
query strings, encoded paths, case and trailing-slash variants
assets, APIs, sitemap, robots and localized canonical routes

sources.label: VII accepted product and release standard

midpoint_gate.trigger: Complete classification of the legacy sitemap and current catalog before changing production routing
checks: every legacy sitemap URL has exactly one disposition
semantic equivalents are supported by catalog or explicit route evidence
obsolete URLs are 410 rather than home redirects
targets are final canonical URLs with no chains
Search Console inventory gaps are recorded before release

attack_questions: Does any old sitemap URL still return 200 old content or 404 after cutover?
Does any redirect land on the home page without semantic equivalence?
Does any source require more than one redirect hop or loop?
Can an enabled admin 301 or 410 be observed on the public worker?
Do assets, APIs, robots, sitemap and localized pages remain unaffected?
Does the exact live old hostname prove the release rather than only the temporary hostname?
adversarial_close.natural_destination_evidence: Live HTTP matrix from representative and randomly sampled legacy URLs on both old hostnames, ending at final public canonicals on the exact deployed release.
adversarial_close.affected_family_evidence: Machine-readable full inventory audit plus build/tests, Search Console evidence, sitemap/robots verification and rollback identity.

effectiveness.baseline: The legacy domain still serves the old site; the new worker only has partial catalog-derived 308 mappings and does not execute D1-managed redirect records.
effectiveness.target: 100 percent of collected legacy sitemap URLs classified, every valid equivalent redirected in one 301 hop, every no-equivalent URL intentionally 410, and live old-host verification after publication.
